subject: history_social
passage: In January 1913, Srinivasa Ramanujan, a clerk in Madras with little formal training in advanced mathematics, mailed several pages of theorems to the Cambridge mathematician G. H. Hardy. Some of the results were already known, but others were unlike anything Hardy had seen. After studying the pages with his colleague J. E. Littlewood, Hardy had to decide whether their author was a crank or a ______ soon concluded the latter and invited Ramanujan to Cambridge, where the two began one of the most productive partnerships in the history of mathematics.
stem: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?

explanation.why: "Hardy had to decide whether their author was a crank or a genius" is a statement that reports a question indirectly; it is not itself a question, so it ends with a period. "He soon concluded the latter ..." is a new independent clause, so it must begin a new sentence (or be properly joined).
explanation.A: Incorrect. A comma alone can't join the two independent clauses; this is a comma splice.
explanation.B: Correct. The period ends the statement containing the indirect question, and "He soon concluded the latter" begins a new sentence.
explanation.C: Incorrect. With no punctuation, the two independent clauses run together as a run-on sentence.
explanation.D: Incorrect. An indirect question introduced by "whether" is part of a statement, so it ends with a period, not a question mark.
